members.name: closing_auction_anticipation_v1
members.thesis: NSE's closing auction (15:30-15:40) concentrates 5-8% of daily volume. Stocks trending in a direction during the last 30 minutes tend to continue into the close as index fund rebalancing, mutual fund NAV-related orders, and institutional closing trades cluster. By entering at 15:00 in the direction
weaknesses: Very short hold (29 bars max) — edge per trade is thin; need high frequency to compound
Closing 30 min can be unpredictable on news days — institutional flow gets disrupted
Must flatten by 15:29 — can't capture the actual auction premium without overnight exposure
members.prior_art: Closing auction premium — documented in market microstructure literature (Pagano et al.)

members.name: pre_market_auction_edge_v1
members.thesis: NSE pre-market auction (09:00-09:08) sets indicative prices that often differ from the continuous session opening price at 09:15. When the auction equilibrium price (AEP) is > 0.2% above/below the previous close AND the first 5 bars of continuous trading confirm the direction, a strong intraday move
filters: AEP direction must align with first-5-bar direction
weaknesses: Pre-market auction data availability via Zerodha API is limited — may need alternative data source
AEP can differ significantly from continuous open if auction participation is low
Opening minutes have highest slippage — 4+ bps typical
members.prior_art: Pre-market auction analysis — NSE-specific, less studied in academic literature

members.name: last_30_min_momentum_v1
members.thesis: Stocks that are up/down > 1% for the day with sustained volume tend to accelerate in the last 30 minutes (14:45-15:15) as institutional portfolio managers who have been monitoring all day make final positioning decisions.
